note: Partial bank: only questions on G12 Maths Unit 1 (sequences and series) and Unit 2 (calculus). ESSLCE Mathematics for Natural Science, Tikimt 2015 E.C. (printed '2014/15; October 2022'), the 2014 E.C. exam — key-p1.pdf pp. 344–353, solutions pp. 364–377

items.text: Which one of the following is the derivative of f(x) = tan x + 3^x?
items.why:
1) d/dx(tan x) = sec²x.
2) d/dx(a^x) = a^x ln a, so d/dx(3^x) = 3^x ln 3.
3) f′(x) = sec²x + 3^x ln 3.
4) None of the options matches: B has ln x instead of ln 3, C omits ln 3, A and D have the wrong derivative of tan x.
topics: derivative of tan x and exponential
items.review: The book gives 'No Answer'. Agreed: the correct derivative sec²x + 3^x ln 3 is not among the options (B was probably meant to read ln 3).

items.text: The sum of the first 8 terms of a geometric sequence with first term 0.3 and common ratio 1/10 is equal to:
What is the seventh term of an arithmetic sequence whose third term is −4 and common difference is 5?
What is the derivative of the function f(x) = xe^x / cos x at x = 0?
items.why:
1) Quotient rule with u = xe^x, v = cos x: f′ = (u′v − uv′)/v².
2) u′ = e^x + xe^x, v′ = −sin x.
3) At x = 0: u = 0, u′ = 1, v = 1, v′ = 0.
4) f′(0) = (1·1 − 0·0)/1² = 1.

items.text: Let f and g be two functions. Which one of the following is true?
opts: A. If f is differentiable at a, then f is continuous at a.
B. The line y = 0 is a tangent line to the graph of f(x) = |x| at (0, 0).
C. If f and g are differentiable at a, then f/g is differentiable at a.
D. If f′(a) = 0, then the tangent line to the graph of f at (a, f(a)) is y = a.
items.why:
1) A is a theorem: differentiability at a implies continuity at a.
2) B false: |x| has a corner at 0 (left slope −1, right slope 1), so no tangent line there.
3) C false: f/g needs g(a) ≠ 0 (e.g. g(x) = x at a = 0).
4) D false: the horizontal tangent is y = f(a), not y = a.

items.text: Suppose f is a twice continuously differentiable function and f″(3) = 5. If g(x) = f(2x + 3), then what is the second derivative of g at 0?
If the perimeter of a rectangle is 120 m, what are the length l and width w maximizing its area?
Suppose f is a continuous function on the interval [a, b] and differentiable on (a, b), and f(a) = f(b). Which one of the following must be true?
opts: A. f has a minimum value in (a, b).
B. f has a zero in (a, b).
C. The graph of f has a horizontal tangent at (c, f(c)) for some c ∈ (a, b).
D. f has a maximum value in (a, b).
items.why:
1) The hypotheses are those of Rolle's theorem, so f′(c) = 0 for some c ∈ (a, b).
2) f′(c) = 0 means a horizontal tangent at (c, f(c)) — C.
3) A need not hold: f(x) = sin x on [0, π] takes its minimum only at the endpoints. D need not hold: f(x) = −sin x on [0, π] takes its maximum only at the endpoints. B fails for f(x) = 2 + sin x on [0, π] (never zero).

items.text: Let f be continuous on ℝ and c be a number in the domain of f. Which one of the following must be true?
opts: A. If f(c) is a local minimum value of f, then f′(c) = 0.
B. An absolute maximum value of f which is attained at a critical number is also a local maximum value of f.
C. If c is a critical number of f, then f(c) is a local extreme value.
D. If f″(c) = 0, then (c, f(c)) is an inflection point.
items.why:
1) A false: f(x) = |x| has a local minimum at 0 but f′(0) does not exist.
2) C false: f(x) = x³ has critical number 0 but no extremum there.
3) D false: f(x) = x⁴ has f″(0) = 0 but no inflection point (concave up on both sides).
4) B true: an absolute maximum at an interior point of ℝ is, in particular, the largest value near c, so it is a local maximum.
topics: critical points, local and absolute extrema

items.text: Which one of the following is true about a bounded sequence?
opts: A. Every decreasing bounded sequence converges to the least upper bound.
B. Every monotonic bounded sequence converges.
C. Every bounded sequence is convergent.
D. Every increasing bounded sequence converges to the greatest lower bound.
items.why:
1) Monotone convergence theorem: a monotonic and bounded sequence converges — B.
2) A false: a decreasing bounded sequence converges to its greatest lower bound (infimum), not the least upper bound.
3) C false: (−1)ⁿ is bounded but does not converge.
4) D false: an increasing bounded sequence converges to its least upper bound (supremum).

items.text: What is the value of ∫_{0}^{1} xe^x dx?
items.why:
1) Integration by parts: u = x, dv = e^x dx ⇒ du = dx, v = e^x.
2) ∫xe^x dx = xe^x − ∫e^x dx = xe^x − e^x + C.
3) [xe^x − e^x]_0^1 = (e − e) − (0 − 1) = 1.

items.review: Book key C is wrong. In its solution the book writes 5·x^(−1)/(−1) but then records +5/x; the correct term is −5/x, so the answer is D (verified by differentiating).

items.text: Let f be continuous on [a, b]. Which one of the following is NOT true?
opts: A. ∫_{a}^{b} f(x) dx = ∫_{a}^{c} f(x) dx − ∫_{c}^{b} f(x) dx for any c in (a, b)
B. ∫_{c}^{c} f(x) dx = 0 for any c in (a, b)
D. ∫_{a}^{b} k f(x) dx = k ∫_{a}^{b} f(x) dx
items.why:
1) Additivity: ∫_a^b f = ∫_a^c f + ∫_c^b f (a plus sign), so A is NOT true.
2) B: an integral over an interval of zero length is 0 (true).
3) C: reversing the limits changes the sign (true).
4) D: constants can be taken outside the integral (true).
(Option B's right-hand side is partly cut off in the scan; the standard property ∫_c^c f = 0 is assumed.)
